柳笛傳統以綠色柳枝剝下的樹皮段製成，現代多用塑膠，常見聚氯乙烯管。卡累利阿變體製: The willow flute is traditionally made from a tube of bark peeled from a green willow branch; today it is mostly plastic, commonly a PVC pipe. The Karelian variant is made the same way but uses birch bark. The kalyuka tradition makes it from hollow plant stems such as motherwort or angelica, and today mostly from PVC. The mouthpiece consists of a notched plug pushed into the end of the tube and a cut in the tube wall; the plug's material is not stated.
柳笛屬氣鳴泛音笛，無指孔。吹奏時將氣流吹入橫置哨口，以手指遮蓋或開放管端，並改變: The willow flute is an aerophonic overtone flute with no fingerholes. The player blows into the transverse whistle mouth, covers or opens the end of the tube with a finger and changes the strength of the breath to obtain different fundamentals and their overtones. What a beginner has to learn is not fingering but a steady airstream and control of the open and closed end; because the sound follows the harmonic series it cannot play an equal-tempered scale. The Russian and Ukrainian kalyuka variant partly covers the top end with the tongue and opens and closes the bottom or a side hole, and reaches the high notes by overblowing.
柳笛常見於北歐民間音樂與傳統編制，也見於俄羅斯、烏克蘭的泛音笛傳統。卡累利阿變體: The willow flute is common in Nordic folk music and traditional line-ups, and is also found in the overtone-flute traditions of Russia and Ukraine. The Karelian variant is used by the Karelian folk music ensemble based in Petrozavodsk. In East European tradition the kalyuka is mostly played in the evening after the summer mowing, with percussion accompaniment. Modern players include Anders Norudde of Sweden, and several Nordic groups that use the instrument in traditional line-ups.

The player selects overtones by changing the strength of the airstream and covers or opens the end of the tube with a finger, obtaining two sets of fundamentals and overtones; the source does not state a specific range or volume. Compared with the related kalyuka, the willow flute changes pitch by its transverse whistle mouth and the open or closed end, while the kalyuka partly closes the top with the tongue and opens and closes the bottom or a small side hole, reaching the high notes by overblowing.

The willow flute (Seljefløyte) is an aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 421.221.11, belonging to the Nordic folk flute and whistle family of overtone flutes. It is a simple tube with no fingerholes, with a notched plug fitted into one end and the mouth cut close beside it; in playing, changes in the strength of the breath and the covering or opening of the end of the tube produce different fundamentals and harmonic series, and a twelve-note equal-tempered scale cannot be played. The tradition is found in Russia, Ukraine, Norway, Sweden, Finland and elsewhere; the Karelian variant is made of birch bark and used by a Karelian folk music group.
此類柳笛為北歐民間氣鳴泛音笛，見於俄羅斯、烏克蘭、挪威、瑞典、芬蘭，另有波蘭農民: Flutes of this kind are Nordic folk aerophonic overtone flutes, found in Russia, Ukraine, Norway, Sweden and Finland, while Polish peasants make a similar instrument by another method. The Karelian variant is made of birch bark and used by the Karelian folk music group of Petrozavodsk. Early instruments were made from the bark of green willow in spring, which cannot be blown once dry; today a plastic pipe (PVC) is mostly used. The kalyuka tradition of Russia and Ukraine was discovered in 1980 by students of the Moscow and St Petersburg conservatories.
